svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Nightseam 0.6.0 — the projection stages and their interfaces
svg.desc: One declaration is rendered into a Go and a TypeScript realization. In each, the generated packages carry a native model to an adapter boundary, which presents the model as a wire. The wire is Bitwire's shared access contract — Wire, Endpoint and Receiver — owned outside both realizations; each realizes it with its peer's endpoint, its channels and its model endpoints, and composes a dispatcher above it. The live and tunnel layers compose over the peer; the peer speaks the profile's frames over a connection of the seam. The two realizations meet at the frames on the wire. A connection, a channel, a selection, a mount and a forward are each a wire again.
svg.text: one declaration, one contract, one profile — each shared, each realized twice; every layer speaks the one beneath it and knows nothing of those above

Wire { send(path, message) } · Endpoint extends Wire { receive(receiver) → detach, close(code, reason) } · Receiver { message(path, message), closed(code, reason) }
a ReturnAddress carries send-only Wire; one owning receive attachment per Endpoint; registration, prefix routing and precedence are a composed dispatcher's, not the contract's

what crosses: request · response · event · cancel, with the meta header and trace context; the reserved vocabularies channel.* live.* identity.* as ordinary frames;
request serials that increase per direction; the declaration's digest at channel.open, at identity.check and on a transferred reference — never a path member, never a lifecycle verb
the recurrence — and where the layers meet it
a connection is a wire at [] · a tunnel channel is a wire, being a connection of the seam · at(w, p), mount({…}) and forward(w) yield a wire again
a model adapter targets a wire — ToWire(model) → Endpoint, FromWire(endpoint) → model — so a selected part and an assembled whole are used the same way
a live reference names a binding in a scope, beside the wire, under an owner the caller supplies; the conformance suite holds every language to this one definition
